title: NEBExpress Ni Resin Gravity Flow Protocol
author: New England Biolabs
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfd7ji9n

steps.title: Prepare Buffers for Denaturing Conditions
steps.instruction: If using denaturing conditions, adjust the Lysis/Binding, Wash, and Elution Buffers to a final concentration of 8 M Urea or 6 M Guanidine.

steps.title: Harvest Cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4000 x g for 15 minutes. Store the pellet at -20 °C or process immediately.

substeps.instruction: Pre-weigh the vessel prior to adding cell suspension to determine the mass of the cell pellet used.

steps.title: Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in Lysis buffer (approximately 5 mL per 1 g of cell paste) and lyse using the method of choice (e.g., sonication, repeated freeze-thaw cycles, French press, or commercial reagents).

substeps.instruction: Ensure imidazole is omitted from the lysis buffer.

steps.title: Clarify Protein Lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 12000 x g for 15 minutes to pellet cellular debris.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the clarified protein lysate supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Retain an aliquot of the clarified lysate for SDS-PAGE analysis.

steps.title: Prepare Ni Resin Column
steps.instruction: Resuspend the Ni Resin slurry by gently shaking the bottle and transfer the desired amount to a closed column, allowing the resin to settle.

substeps.instruction: Open the column and allow the storage buffer to flow through.

steps.title: Equilibrate Resin
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the resin by adding 5 column volumes (CV) of Lysis/Binding buffer and allowing it to flow through.

steps.title: Load Protein Sample
steps.instruction: Load the protein sample lysate onto the column and allow it to interact with the resin for ≥ 00:05:00.

substeps.instruction: Collect the flow through in a clean tube and reserve for SDS-PAGE analysis.
If extending binding time to maintain protein activity, place the column at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash Column
steps.instruction: Add ≥ 10 CV of Wash buffer to the column and allow it to flow through.

substeps.instruction: Monitor flow through with absorbance at 280 nm to ensure complete removal of unbound lysate effluent.
Collect flow through in fractions and reserve for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Optionally increase imidazole in wash buffer to 15 mM to minimize contaminants.

steps.title: Elute Fusion Protein
steps.instruction: Elute the target protein using Elution buffer, using a minimum of 3 CV.

substeps.instruction: Monitor protein elution by measuring absorbance at 280 nm or by SDS-PAGE.

steps.title: Analyze Samples
steps.instruction: Analyze the protein sample lysate (load), flow through, washes, and eluates by SDS-PAGE.

substeps.instruction: If imidazole removal is required for downstream applications, use gel filtration (e.g., Zeba Spin Desalting Columns) or dialysis (e.g., slide-A-Lyzer Dialysis Cassettes).

steps.title: Clean Resin Column
steps.instruction: Determine flow rate prior to cleaning. Choose one of the following methods based on the contaminant to be removed:

substeps.instruction: To remove lipoproteins, lipids, and hydrophobic proteins: Add 1 M NaOH (contact time 01:00:00 to 02:00:00), followed by 10 CV of Lysis/Binding Buffer; OR add 30% isopropanol (contact time 00:15:00 - 00:20:00), followed by 10 CV of water; OR add 0.1–0.5% non-ionic detergent in 0.1 M acetic acid (contact time 01:00:00 – 02:00:00), followed by 10 CV of water.
To remove proteins bound by ionic interactions: Add 1.5 M NaCl (contact time 00:10:00 – 00:15:00), followed by 10 CV of water.

steps.title: Store Resin
steps.instruction: For long-term storage, store NEBExpress Ni Resin in 20% ethanol at 2 °C – 8 °C.
